A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KNOW/KNOWN work, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. However, neither includes its referenced implementation appendix, and v2 additionally references unavailable supplementary analysis. The supplied main papers support reliable comparison; the referenced supplements do not.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, domain-generalization, captioning and segmentation experiments, plus ablation and timing results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional comparator results in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The documented procedure retains progressive subset fine-tuning, reverse weight prediction, the 9,425-parameter two-stream KNOWN architecture, operation-specific predictors, L1 training objective and iterative forecasting. Reordering and explanatory revisions do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: The reported meta-training datasets and classification, PACS domain-generalization, Flickr8K captioning and VOC-to-Cityscapes segmentation coverage remain the same. Incremental pretraining changes the procedure within existing coverage; revised dataset citations alone do not establish different evaluated data.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds incremental pretraining, ConsensusTA, MagMax and TSV. Tables 2–5 add TSV at ×3 and ×9 and MagMax at ×9, substantially broadening the comparison methods. Footnotes identify several lower-step ConsensusTA/MagMax cases as equivalent to TaskVector.

E3.justification: v2 adds an incremental-pretraining control using progressively increasing data from 6.25% to 100%, followed by transfer without KNOW. Existing experiments retain their reported dataset fractions, prediction factors, training schedules and metrics; omitted PACS implementation details do not establish a changed protocol.

E4.justification: Table 1 adds the incremental-pretraining control, while the visible S ablation, dataset-size study, landscape visualization, segmentation cases and timing analysis are retained. v2 refers the diagnostic explanation of overfitted initialization to unavailable supplementary material, preventing reliable assessment of the scope and substance of that added analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten repetitions and report results with ± values. v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting procedure, significance test or explicit increase in repetitions; changed numerical uncertainty values belong to E6.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 contain substantial new comparator results. Retained KNOWN entries also change: Table 2 CUB ×3 changes from 70.97 ± 0.67 to 71.18 ± 0.45, and Cars ×9 from 88.51 ± 0.17 to 88.85 ± 0.23. PACS and captioning entries receive smaller updates. Existing Table 1 entries and Tables 6–7 results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The forgetting preliminary, inverse-forgetting existence hypothesis, nested-dataset formulation, Equations 1–6 and geometric time-cost expression retain their mathematical content. Boxing statements and relocating the conceptual justification add no theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that reversing structured forgetting produces knowledge-enriched initializations and that KNOWN generalizes across architectures and downstream tasks without further meta-training. The stronger emphasis on practical data constraints clarifies the motivation without changing these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 newly attributes incremental-pretraining underperformance to overfitted initialization and explicitly directs readers to assess gains relative to Naïve Transfer. The cited supplementary support for that causal explanation is unavailable. Existing interpretations of nonlinear forgetting trajectories and transferability are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/pretrained-model access statement and implementation descriptions for new comparators, including TSV's top-10% singular components and ConsensusTA/MagMax selection rules. It removes v1's explicit PACS Adam-optimizer and augmentation details. Neither supplied PDF includes the referenced implementation appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for TSV, MagMax, ConsensusTA and pedestrian detection, and replaces several dataset references. Its foundational positioning around weight nowcasting, meta-learning and inverse forgetting remains substantially unchanged; bibliographic publication updates are not new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 revises introductory and experimental prose, moves transfer learning from Section 4.6 to 4.2 and qualitative validation from 5.2 to 4.7, and integrates Section 6.3's justification into Section 3. The overall narrative and main section structure remain recognizable; title wording, affiliations and acknowledgements also receive edits.

P2.justification: Existing Tables 1–5 expand with comparator rows and explanatory footnotes. v2 boxes the preliminary and hypotheses, resizes or relocates existing figures and tables, and reformats Table 7. The four figures retain their underlying visual content; no new figure-based analysis appears.

improvement.justification: The incremental-pretraining control and additional model-merging comparisons address v1's narrower comparator coverage, while the code/model pointer improves reproducibility documentation. These are modest gains. Supplementary diagnostic support remains unavailable, and v2 introduces a misleading Table 1 caption implying that incremental pretraining uses KNOW despite the methods text stating otherwise.
